source_text: Sed quoniam tam expedita probatio est, ut, si statim proferatur, nihil iam sit retractandum, ac si prolata non sit a nobis, locum interim demus diversae parti, si quid putant ad infirmandam hanc praescriptionem movere se posse, solent dicere non omnia apostolos scisse, eadem agitati dementia qua susum rursus convertunt omnia quidem apostolos scisse, sed non omnia omnibus tradidisse, in utroque Christum reprehensioni inicientes, qui aut minus instructos aut parum simplices apostolos miserit. Quis igitur integrae mentis credere potest aliquid eos ignorasse quos magistros dominus dedit, individuos habens in comitatu, in discipulatu, in convictu, quibus obscura quaeque seorsum disserebat, illis dicens datum esse cognoscere arcana, quae populo intellegere non liceret? Latuit aliquid Petrum aedificandae ecclesiae petram dictum, claves regni caelorum consecutum et solvendi et alligandi in caelis et in terris potestatem? Latuit et Ioannem aliquid, dilectissimum domino, pectori eius incubantem, cui soli dominus Iudam traditorem praemonstravit, quem loco suo filium Mariae demandavit? Quid eos ignorasse voluit quibus etiam gloriam suam exhibuit et Moysen et Helian et insuper de caelo patris vocem? non quasi ceteros reprobans, sed quoniam in tribus testibus stabit omne verbum. Ignoraverunt itaque et illi quibus post resurrectionem quoque in itinere omnes scripturas edisserere dignatus est. Dixerat plane aliquando, Multa habeo adhuc loqui vobis, sed non potestis modo ea sustinere, tamen adiciens, Cum venerit ille spiritus veritatis, ipse vos deducet in omnem veritatem. Ostendit illos nihil ignorasse quos omnem veritatem consecuturos per spiritum veritatis promiserat. Et utique implevit repromissum, probantibus Actis Apostolorum descensum spiritus sancti. Quam scripturam qui non recipiunt, nec spiritus sancti esse possunt, qui necdum spiritum sanctum possunt agnoscere discentibus missum, sed nec ecclesiam se dicant defendere, qui quando et quibus incunabulis institutum est hoc corpus probare non habent. Tanti est enim illis non habere probationes eorum quae defendunt, ne pariter admittantur traductiones eorum quae mentiuntur.
thought_title: The apostles knew all truth and passed it on
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who claim the apostles either did not know everything or did not hand on everything, in order to weaken his legal objection that heretics have no right to the Scriptures.
pass_a_gloss: But since the proof is so ready that, if it is brought forward at once, nothing remains to be reconsidered, and if it has not been brought forward by us, let us for the time being give place to the opposing side, if they think they can move anything to weaken this legal objection. They are accustomed to say that the apostles did not know all things, driven by the same madness by which they turn back again upward to say that the apostles did know all things, but did not hand on all things to all people, in both cases casting reproach upon Christ, who sent apostles either too little instructed or too little simple. Who therefore of sound mind can believe that they were ignorant of anything, whom the Lord gave as teachers, holding them inseparable in his company, in his discipleship, in his daily life, to whom he explained all obscure things separately, saying to them that it was given to know the hidden things which the people were not permitted to understand? Did anything lie hidden from Peter, called the rock of the church to be built, who obtained the keys of the kingdom of heaven and the power of loosing and binding in heaven and on earth? Did anything lie hidden from John, most beloved by the Lord, leaning on his breast, to whom alone the Lord pointed out Judas the betrayer, whom in his own place he entrusted as son of Mary? What did he wish them to have been ignorant of, to whom he also showed his glory and Moses and Elijah and in addition the voice of the Father from heaven? Not as if rejecting the rest, but because every word will stand on three witnesses. Therefore they also were not ignorant, to whom after the resurrection also on the road he deigned to explain all the Scriptures. He had indeed said at some time, I have many things still to say to you, but you cannot bear them now, yet adding, When that spirit of truth comes, he himself will lead you into all truth. He showed that they were ignorant of nothing, whom he had promised to attain all truth through the spirit of truth. And certainly he fulfilled the promise, as the Acts of the Apostles prove the descent of the Holy Spirit. Those who do not receive this Scripture cannot be of the Holy Spirit either, who cannot yet recognize the Holy Spirit sent to the disciples, but let them not say they defend the church, who do not have the means to prove when and with what beginnings this body was established. For it is worth so much to them not to have proofs of the things they defend, lest the tracings of the things they falsely claim be admitted equally.

choices.why: The glossary requires this rendering for praescriptio, the technical legal term central to the whole treatise.
Tertullian uses this strong word to characterize the heretics' contradictory claims; 'madness' preserves the force.
The word refers to the secret truths Jesus explained privately to the disciples; 'hidden things' keeps the sense of what is concealed from the people.
The image is of a cradle or earliest origin; 'beginnings' conveys the point that heretics cannot show the church's founding.
The word means a tracing back or derivation of lineage; 'tracings' preserves the idea of a line of transmission that heretics cannot produce.

pass_b_english: But the proof is so easy that if it were brought forward at once, nothing would remain to be reconsidered. And if we have not brought it forward, let us for the moment give room to the opposing side, in case they think they can raise anything to weaken this legal objection. They are in the habit of saying that the apostles did not know everything. They are driven by the same madness with which they turn things back again and say that the apostles did know everything, but did not hand on everything to everyone. In both cases they cast blame on Christ, who sent apostles either too poorly instructed or too little straightforward.

Who, then, of sound mind can believe that those men were ignorant of anything? The Lord gave them as teachers, keeping them inseparable in his company, in his discipleship, in his daily life. To them he explained every obscure matter privately, saying to them that it was given to them to know hidden things which the people were not permitted to understand. Did anything escape Peter, who was called the rock of the church to be built, who obtained the keys of the kingdom of heaven and the power of loosing and binding in heaven and on earth? Did anything escape John, the Lord's most beloved, leaning on his breast, to whom alone the Lord pointed out Judas the betrayer beforehand, whom he entrusted to Mary as a son in his own place? What did he want them to be ignorant of, those to whom he also showed his glory and Moses and Elijah, and above all the Father's voice from heaven? Not as if he rejected the others, but because every word will stand on three witnesses.

So they were ignorant, were they, those for whom after the resurrection too he deigned to explain all the Scriptures on the road? He had indeed said at one time, 'I have many things still to say to you, but you cannot bear them now,' yet he added, 'When that spirit of truth comes, he himself will lead you into all truth.' He showed that they were ignorant of nothing, since he had promised that they would attain all truth through the spirit of truth. And he certainly fulfilled his promise, as the Acts of the Apostles prove by the descent of the Holy Spirit.

Those who do not receive this writing cannot be of the Holy Spirit either, since they cannot yet recognize that the Holy Spirit was sent to the disciples. Nor should they claim to defend the church, since they have no way to prove when and with what beginnings this body was established. For it matters that much to them not to have proofs for the things they defend, lest the tracings of the things they falsely claim be admitted along with them.

problems.quote: tracings of the things they falsely claim
problems.why: Latin 'traductiones' means 'translations', not 'tracings'; the English changes the meaning.
problems.fix: translations of the things they falsely claim

problems.quote: whom in his own place he entrusted as a son to Mary
problems.source_quote: quem loco suo filium Mariae demandavit
problems.why: The Latin does not say John was made a son of Mary; the English adds a nonsensical relationship.
problems.fix: whom, in his own place, he called the son of Mary
problems.ruling: "filium Mariae" = Mary's son; "loco suo" = in his place. Christ entrusted Mary's son (John) to her, not John as a son to Mary.

fixed: Changed 'entrusted as a son to Mary' to 'called the son of Mary' for 'filium Mariae demandavit'.

problems.quote: lest the translations of the things they falsely claim be admitted along with them.
problems.why: 'Translations' does not fit the context; the argument concerns claims or traditions, not translations.

problems.quote: whom, in his own place, he called the son of Mary
problems.why: This appears to conflate Judas with James, son of Mary (Mark 15:40); the reference is unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify which biblical event is being referenced.
